name: Gouda Chickpea Pasta with Chicken and Spinach
subtitle: Chickpea pasta in a gouda and Jack cheese sauce with seared chicken and a lot of spinach

macros.portion: About 2 cups pasta with chicken and spinach.
macros.note: Rough estimate from standard nutrition values for the listed amounts, not a lab number.

before: Chicken tenderloins thawed in the fridge (1 day).
notes: An aged gouda tastes great but doesn't melt smoothly on its own: past a few months it loses moisture, and in a hot sauce the fat separates and turns grainy. So the sauce is built on evaporated milk thickened with cornstarch, which keeps cheese emulsified, with Monterey Jack doing most of the melting and part of the gouda for flavor. The rest of the gouda is grated over the top at the end. Add cheese off the heat, a handful at a time. Chickpea pasta goes from done to mushy fast and keeps softening in the sauce, so pull it 2 minutes before the package time. It foams a lot while boiling; use the large pot.

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt, for the water

steps.title: Water on
steps.body: Fill the large pot with water, add **1 Tbsp kosher salt**, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat.

steps.title: Spinach
steps.body: While the water heats: microwave **2 bags frozen spinach** in a bowl **4–5 min** until thawed. When cool enough to handle, squeeze it hard in a clean towel until it stops dripping. Into a bowl.

steps.title: Chicken, cheese and sauce prep
steps.body: Cut **1¼ lb chicken tenderloins** into 1-inch pieces and toss with **½ tsp salt** and **¼ tsp pepper**. Grate **2 oz Monterey Jack** and **3 oz aged gouda** on the fine side of a box grater; keep **1 oz gouda** in a separate small bowl for the top. Mince **3 cloves garlic**. In a measuring cup, whisk **1 can evaporated milk** with **1 Tbsp cornstarch**, **1 tsp Dijon** and **¼ tsp pepper** until smooth.

steps.title: Staging check
steps.body: Within reach: chicken, **1 Tbsp olive oil**, garlic, the milk mixture (whisk again before using), both cheese bowls, spinach, the pasta, a measuring cup for pasta water, a colander, tongs and a spatula.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.body: Skillet over medium-high. Add **1 Tbsp olive oil**, then the chicken in one layer. Leave **2 min** until browned, then stir and cook 3–4 min more until no longer pink inside. Move to a plate.

steps.title: Pasta in
steps.body: Add **10 oz chickpea pasta** to the boiling water. Set a timer for **2 min less** than the package says. Stir now and then; turn the heat down a little if it foams up.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.body: While the pasta cooks: skillet over medium-low. Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds. Whisk the milk mixture again and pour it in. Stir constantly until it bubbles at the edges and thickens enough to coat a spoon, 2–3 min. Turn the heat **off**. Add the Jack and the 2 oz gouda a handful at a time, stirring until each melts.

steps.title: Drain
steps.body: Scoop out **½ cup pasta water**, then drain the pasta. Don't rinse.

steps.title: Combine
steps.body: Add the pasta, chicken and spinach to the sauce and toss on low heat **1 min**. Loosen with pasta water a splash at a time until it's creamy rather than tight. Off heat, grate or scatter the **1 oz gouda** over the top.

after: Pack lunches with a splash of water over each portion; chickpea pasta absorbs the sauce overnight. Reheat at 50% power, stirring halfway.

source.label: Evaporated-milk cheese sauce method, adapted for an aged gouda
